headline: Find the pair. Remember the past.
statement: Given an integer array nums and target, return the two distinct indices whose values sum to target. Exactly one pair exists; either index order is valid.
constraints: Values and target are integers between -10^9 and 10^9
Exactly one valid pair; an element cannot pair with itself
intuition: Remember the numbers already visited so each new number can ask for its missing partner. A lookup replaces an entire inner search.
approach: Create an empty map from value to earlier index.
At index i, compute target - nums[i]. Check the map before recording nums[i].
If the complement exists, return its stored index and i; otherwise record the current value.
correctness: Before processing i, the map contains only indices smaller than i. A found complement therefore uses distinct elements and sums to target. For the guaranteed pair, its later element finds the earlier one.
bruteForce: Try every pair i < j: O(n²) time and O(1) extra space.

complexity.explanation: Hash-map operations take expected constant time, giving O(n) expected time and O(n) auxiliary storage. Pathological collisions can worsen the time bound.

pitfalls: Record after lookup, or target = 2*x could reuse one element.
Negative numbers work without a special case.
